learning_outcomes.text: That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Knowledge and capacities for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Knowledge and capacities for the application of materials engineering.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I: TOPOGRAPHY

Introduction to Topography. Fundamental concepts. Representation of topographic surfaces. System of scaled planes. Geodesy. Reference Systems. Angles and distances. Calculation and transformation of coordinates.
Fundamental Principles. The Earth: figure and dimensions. Cartographic projections.
Error Theory. Introduction. Classification of errors. Direct measurements.
Topographic Instruments. Expedited instrumentation. Topographic instruments. Common elements. Levels. Indirect distance measurement. Theodolites-tachyometers. Electronic distance measurement.
Topographic Methods. Planimetric methods. Altimetric methods.
GNSS System. Satellite positioning and navigation.
BLOCK II: CONSTRUCTION MATERIALS
Construction Materials. Concept of construction material. Evolution. Quality of construction materials and their control. Sustainable construction materials and applications.
Wood. Introduction. Structure and properties. Treatments. Manufacturing process. Durability. Tests. Applications.

Ceramic Materials. Introduction. General aspects. Classification. Mechanical and thermal properties. Commercial forms, description and properties. Bricks. Tiles. Azulejos and Gres. Refractories. Glasses. Defects and alterations. Tests.

Metals and Alloys. Introduction. Generalities and properties. Processing of metallic materials. Cast irons. Steels. Aluminum and its alloys. Copper and its alloys. Oxidation and corrosion. Protection against corrosion.

Cement and Concrete. Introduction. Portland cement. Types of cements. Classifications. Production. Mechanical properties. Durability. Binders. Additives. Classifications and types. Concrete. Mixtures and production. Special concretes. Deterioration and its prevention. Inspection and tests.

Bituminous Materials. Introduction. Nature. Components of bituminous materials. Viscosity, stiffness and deformation. Resistance, failure and durability. Production. Inspection and control. Applications.

Polymeric Materials. Concepts. Classification. Processing of plastic materials. Manufacturing. Mechanical and thermal properties. Degradation and durability. Inspection and tests. Selection and design criteria. Applications.
PRACTICES
Calculation and transformation of coordinates.
Surveying.
Radiation.
Geometric leveling.
Trigonometric leveling.
GNSS.
Granulometric analysis of aggregates.
Characterization of bricks.
Binders and conglomerates.
Determination of the apparent density of cement.
Cement testing method. Determination of setting time.
Tests of fresh concrete: slump test.
Tests of concrete in structures. Non-destructive tests. Determination of rebound index.
Manufacturing and characterization of asphalt mixtures.
